newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Iran has enormous potential but BP staying out.
newsitem.headline: Iran has enormous potential but BP staying out.

text.p: British Petroleum Plc sees great potential in Iran's oil and gas industry but the global giant said on Saturday it has no immediate plans to invest in the Islamic republic.
"The potential (in Iran) is enormous...But equally the potential that we have presently in BP is enormous," BP's chief executive John Browne told Reuters in Kuwait.
BP is "working in many countries doing lots of things...We must always make choices in where we go and we are making these choices now," he added.
U.S. President Bill Clinton last year signed a sanctions act giving him discretionary power to punish non-American firms that invest $40 million or more a year in Iran's oil and gas sectors.

Washington accuses Tehran of supporting international terrorism and hopes sanctions would bring about a change in Iran's policies towards the West. Tehran denies the accusations and often says the sanctions proved to be a failure.

Browne said BP was not under any political pressure by London or Washington to stay out of Iran -- the world's second largest oil exporter which also controls the barely tapped second largest natural gas reserves in the world.
"We are not active in Iran, other companies are," Browne said of competitors like France's Total SA which are involved in major projects in Iran.

Earlier this month executives from global giants like Total, Gaz de France, Elf Aquitaine, British Gas, Agip and Royal Dutch Shell Group flocked to Iran for a two-day gas conference despite the threat of the U.S. sanctions, which were rejected by the European Union.

"This is the big issue about sanctions. Sanctions sometimes do not create the effect that they were expected to have...Where there is a need people will always find a way to find others to work with them," added Browne.

Browne is on a two-day visit to Kuwait to coincide with an official visit by Britain's Prince Charles. Iran's Oil Minister Gholamreza Aghazadeh also arrived in Kuwait earlier on Saturday on a two-day official visit.
